items.why: Pedestrian, cyclist, truck, emergency, and off-road rules are declarative recall served by standard flashcards and quizzes; no separate practice mode is needed.

sections.heading: C - Sharing the Road
sections.markdown:
## C - Sharing the Road

FACT_ID: sec10-F01 | anchor: A01
Everyone owns the road together, so drive courteously and telegraph yourself; stay yield-ready for walkers anywhere, always yield in crosswalks marked or not including signed mid-block ones and to every pedestrian in the intersection even on green, brace for walkers on red turns, crawl past parked rows that hide crossers, scan before backing especially amid crowds, dip under the limit and coil to stop around playgrounds and homes, obey slower school limits when lights flash or children show and halt for patrol signals, while mid-road jaywalkers owe you the yield [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec10-F02 | anchor: A01
Kentucky law yields the road to blind walkers with visible white canes or assistance dogs under a $250 fine, so halt within 5 feet of the crosswalk short of advance bars to stay audible, and mind silent electrics and hybrids [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec10-F03 | anchor: A02
Never talk a blind crosser across since they read traffic sound, never wait them out forever, roll when they step back and pocket the cane, never plug the crosswalk and force a traffic detour, and never honk at their confusion and fright [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec10-F04 | anchor: A02
Bicycles count as vehicles with matching rules, rights, and duties, so respect them, spot their faint profiles, and brace for novices who wobble, blow signs, and ride dark [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec10-F05 | anchor: A02
Yield to bikes in intersections and where paths and lanes cross roads, and keep cars out of bike lanes except for alleys, driveways, official duty, police orders, and true emergencies [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec10-F06 | anchor: A02
Grant cyclists maximum room at low speed, let them clear before you turn, shun sudden slows that overmatch bike brakes, honk only to avert impact, watch lane entries and sidewalk kids, never slice or squeeze them off, expect wrong-way riders, and double care on wet, sandy, or gravelly skin [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec10-F07 | anchor: A02
Non-motor vehicles signal by hand, lamp, or device, flashing intermittently through the last 50 feet before the turn [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec10-F08 | anchor: A03
Cyclists owe hand signals for turns and stops but may grip both bars in trouble, so read head and shoulder tells, door-check for riders before swinging out, and bike-check before backing near schools and homes [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec10-F09 | anchor: A03
Pass bikes slowly with maximum room paced to their speed, holding at least 3 feet and returning right only when well clear, while honoring local bike ordinances [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec10-F10 | anchor: A03
Cyclists shun interstates and parkways, hand-signal, obey every control with full stops, hold posted or reasonable speed, and ride right with traffic [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec10-F11 | anchor: A03
Cyclists yield crosswalks and sidewalks to walkers with a bell or horn warning, light white front and red rear at night, hug the right edge as slow traffic with extreme care when centering for debris, passes, or lefts, never ride sidewalks, never block walkers with parked bikes, and take adjacent paths when built [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec10-F12 | anchor: A04
Bikes carry only their designed souls and ride at most two abreast without fouling traffic [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec10-F13 | anchor: A04
Electric scooters weigh under 100 pounds on wheels with bars and a real brake, carry standers or sitters by motor, muscle, or both up to 20 miles per hour, admit riders 16 and older to roads, lanes, and paths, and obey bike law with bike-grade motorist care [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec10-F14 | anchor: A04
Scooters burn at least one headlamp and one red tail from one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise and in dim times, may sidewalk-park without blocking walkers, and obey every local ordinance [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec10-F15 | anchor: A04
Motorcycles share full road rights and duties yet hide easily, so grant a whole lane always, sweep mirrors and blind spots, study fronts and flanks before lefts, distrust sticky signals until the turn proves real, and trail by 4 seconds or more, longer when wet [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec10-F16 | anchor: A05
Riders jink for potholes, gravel, slicks, seams, rails, and grooves that kill bikers, while scooters and mopeds crawl far below motorcycle pace [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec10-F17 | anchor: A05
Over 250,000 car-commercial crashes strike yearly yet mostly avoidably, since big rigs dwarf cars in size, blind spots, stopping and rolling distances, and turning girth [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec10-F18 | anchor: A05
Side no-zones swallow cars beside tractors and buses, worst on the right from behind the cab down the trailer length, so trade mirror-face sightlines and shun lingering alongside where swerves kill [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec10-F19 | anchor: A05
Front no-zones reflect brutal braking physics, with a loaded 55-mph truck eating at least 335 feet or over 1½ times a car's stopping distance, so never dive ahead or enter before them, passing only once their whole nose fills your mirror at steady speed [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec10-F20 | anchor: A05
Rear no-zones blind trucks to 200 feet behind, so follow loose and mirror-visible with an escape in mind, while grades pin trucks near 35 mph in the right lane, which you should vacate near hills and weigh stations [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec10-F21 | anchor: A06
Honor truck turn signals with wide berth since right turns swing left first, never wedge between rig and curb, wait out the whole turn, meet head-ons hugging far right against sideswipe and shove, turn left only when the rig's speed reads certain, and stop behind set-back lines that bank swing room [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec10-F22 | anchor: A06
Never cut rigs off for exits, turns, or single-lane zones, dodge mountain runaways and shun their escape ramps except as a doomed trucker, queue uphill left and visible with rollback room, dodge weigh-station right lanes, and avoid hazmat haulers that halt at every rail crossing [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec10-F23 | anchor: A06
Siren-and-light rigs own the road, so yield to the edge without plugging intersections for anything flashing red or blue or sounding a siren [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec10-F24 | anchor: A07
At red-blue flashes or siren wails, dive immediately right or curbside clear of intersections and freeze until the emergency passes unless police or fire wave you on, and never tail emergency iron within 500 feet [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec10-F25 | anchor: A07
Pulled over, greet lights and sirens calmly without a travel-lane panic stop, kill the engine, flash hazards plus cabin lights at night, drop the window fully, stay belted with belted passengers, and freeze hands on the wheel instead of pre-fetching papers [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec10-F26 | anchor: A07
On demand, announce each document's spot before slow one-handed retrieval of license, insurance, and registration, answer fully and plainly, stay seated unless extracted, swallow citations without roadside court, obey every order patiently, and never run since chases kill and out-punish tickets [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec10-F27 | anchor: A07
After dismissal, await the officer's cruiser return, scan traffic and the departing patrol car, signal back into flow lawfully per AAMVA stop guidance, while move-over law answers soaring roadside strike tolls by mandating slow-downs and lane shifts with posted reminders [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec10-F28 | anchor: A08
Shouldered emergency iron demands a cautious lane-away shift when traffic allows, else a careful slowdown, with Kentucky adding due caution always, a leftward move on four-lanes when safe, and slow careful passing on two-lanes [A08].
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec10-F29 | anchor: A08
Orange-red rear triangles flag sub-25-mph crawlers, fluorescent orange by day and reflective red rims by night, so approach warily and pass only when safe, granting deaf farm crews crossing and working rural blacktop the same care [A08].
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec10-F30 | anchor: A08
Animal-drawn rigs and horseback riders wield full road rights and duties with fragile bodies, so pass gently without horn or revs that spook mounts, expect field and driveway lefts, and heed posted warning signs [A08].
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec10-F31 | anchor: A08
Kentucky calls ATVs recreational off-road motor vehicles, barring them from public highways, roadways, and rights-of-way save narrow exceptions, so expect the occasional legal ATV and learn the limits before riding [A08].
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec10-F32 | anchor: A09
ATVs need landowner consent anywhere, cabinet-approved helmets whenever rolling on public ground, direct parental eyes plus helmets for under-16 riders, and no knowing passenger loads for unlicensed minors [A09].
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec10-F33 | anchor: A09
ATVs may cross two-lane highways near 90 degrees without riding over 2/10 of a mile, work roads for farm, construction, maintenance, or snow duty, and then only with a valid operator's license, full traffic obedience, one headlight and two taillights blazing, and daylight hours outside snow and emergency repairs [A09].
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0075]
